projectRequirements.name: Workforce Coverage Scheduler
projectRequirements.purpose: Build a useful scheduler for the first company's two IT teams while making organization-specific rules configurable for other businesses. The system proposes schedules, exposes shortages and tradeoffs, and leaves publishing and exceptional decisions to authorized people.

principles.principle: Teams have their own complete schedules, coverage requirements, and configurable rules.
Never silently violate a hard eligibility or assignment rule. A coverage target can remain unmet; show partial coverage accurately.
Cross-team moves must show eligibility and the effect on both source and destination coverage.
Automate roster proposals and repair suggestions while preserving manager control, permissions, and an audit trail.
Show the best recommendation and primary reason first; reveal alternatives and rule details on demand.
The first company's settings are configuration, not special-case code.
Cross-coverage eligibility can depend on agreements and department boundaries as well as qualifications. Policies are versioned, scoped, and explainable.
Schedule by named local time zone and retain exact instants; handle clock changes according to the location's current time-zone rules.

agreedProductModel.term: Demand: dated or repeating time periods, required headcount, skills, mode, team, and importance. No person is assigned here.
Independent employee shifts with person, team, mode, and actual start/end. One shift may satisfy several adjacent Coverage periods; interval intersections determine filled headcount and partial gaps.
agreedProductModel.rule: Coverage uses a repeating weekly team template and dated periods or exceptions. Editing a team template affects newly generated weeks; editing a dated period changes that draft only.

Team preferences define default day/night consistency, on-call grouping, weekend continuity, and preferred block length. Individual preferences can override team defaults. These are soft ranking factors unless a separate hard availability rule applies.

Do not stack full staffed shifts or full standby periods back-to-back by default. Allow staffed duty followed by home/mobile standby where policy permits; distinguish actual call-outs and count their work time for rest review.
agreedProductModel.view: Default to one selected team, remember the selection, and make all-teams grouped view explicit. Add a searchable organization, region, department, and team hierarchy when scale requires it.
Create and edit dated demand periods and inspect partial gaps. Edit repeating patterns on the Teams page.
Create and edit teams, default qualifications, recurring coverage, and team preferences.
Create and edit contact details, home team, qualifications, classification, hard unavailability, and individual preferences.
One-click separate view by team from published shifts; show current and next few contacts with names, phone numbers, start/end times, and unfilled periods.
agreedProductModel.rule: Draft schedule changes and Coverage changes must show affected gaps before publish. Published schedules remain stable until an authorized revised draft is published.

stageOne.item: Two IT teams, approximately 20 employees, with independent schedules and cross-team skill coverage.
Configurable staffed shifts and on-call coverage, including limits on continuous on-call assignment.
Generate draft rosters, allow authorized manual edits, show shortages, and publish schedules.
Compare a small configured set of candidate shift lengths/patterns and explain which covers the weighted demand best under availability and hard limits.
Vacation and other unavailability, including optional weekend endcaps around weekday vacation.
Manager-initiated assignment moves and swaps; explain the effect before approval.
Employee schedule view, scheduler view, administration, and role-scoped access.
Alpha-only automatic sign-in as a seeded master administrator, recreated after database resets; no manual account setup during the first build.
Published-schedule on-call lookup answering who is on call tonight, with coverage hours, team, role, and approved contact details; exportable offline.
Spreadsheet export suitable for importing published shifts into Microsoft Teams Shifts; verify the target template during implementation.
Spreadsheet-like roster, calendar view, coverage indicators, onboarding templates, import validation, and change history.

later.item: More teams, regions, stations, projects, assets, travel distances, radii, travel zones, and geography-aware ranking or eligibility.
Broader automatic discovery of novel and irregular multiweek rotations for large workforces; retain the ability to configure and assign known multiweek patterns before that automation exists.
Employee-initiated swaps, notifications and acknowledgement workflows, richer emergency coverage handling.
Pay rates, premiums, holiday/payroll calculations, payroll administrator workflows and integrations with payroll, SAP, NetSuite, or other systems.
Public business signup and isolated organizations; optional private deployments. Federation between independent instances only if a real use case emerges.
Historical-demand prediction or assisted rule setup only after enough reliable data and a specific benefit are established.
Manager/admin rules builder with enable/disable switches and readable if/then conditions, similar in feel to Outlook rules.

team.name: Team 1
team.note: Interpretation of the original 7-11 and 11-7 shorthand as 7 a.m.-11 p.m. and 11 p.m.-7 a.m. needs confirmation during pilot setup.

pilotConfiguration.note: Coverage counts, required skill combinations, exact shifts, breaks, and employee data remain configurable pilot inputs.

domainModel.entity: Owns configuration and data; designed for isolation between businesses.
Scopes scheduling access and future geographic coverage.
Shift work site or station; employee home base and eligible locations can be recorded from the start.
Own coverage windows, priorities, roster, and transfer policies.
Optional organizational grouping for coverage and movement boundaries, such as grocery, produce, bakery, cashier, or online fulfillment.
Stable external employee ID, employment classification (including full-time and casual), contact visibility, home team/base, availability, preferences, seniority, and memberships.
Organization-defined classification with configurable scheduling targets and eligibility rules; initial examples are full-time and casual.
Optional bargaining unit, agreement, or other policy membership applying to an employee or assignment.
Versioned organization-defined rules scoped to teams, departments, roles, employment groups, locations, and effective dates; distinguish prohibitions, approvals, and preferences.
User-defined skill, role, certification, or experience requirement; examples include team lead, technician, driver, electrician, apprentice, EMR, PCP, and ACP.

Configurable shift durations, start-time windows, days on/off, and repeating multiweek cycles. Examples include 8-hour five-day weeks, 10-hour four-day weeks, 12-hour patterns, and irregular four-week rotations.

An assignable shift with start/end, qualifications, coverage target, location or service time zone, priority band, and scheduling weight; uses the same assignment and publication lifecycle as staffed shifts.
Time window, location or service region, target number, required qualification combinations or distinct slots, and a time-varying coverage weight.

Versioned 0.01-1.00 weights by service region, local day and time interval, team, and optional skill/coverage requirement. Hourly intervals are supported initially; finer granularity can be added later.
Employee, shift or on-call interval, team, location, draft/published status, and change history.
Vacation and other unavailability, with optional adjacent-weekend on-call exclusion.
Role and organization/region/team scope for viewing, editing, approving, and publishing.

bcEmploymentStandardsProfile.rule: Require eight consecutive hours free from work between worked shifts, including work performed during a call-out. Section 36(3) has an emergency exception; a documented variance or applicable exemption must be reviewed separately.

Provide 32 consecutive hours free from work in each seven-day period or the required one-and-a-half-times pay for work during that period. Evaluate rolling seven-day windows and adjacent published weeks, not just a Monday-Sunday display.

Standby at an employer-designated place other than the employee's residence is deemed work. Home/mobile standby is not automatically work, but each actual call-out is work. Store standby location, response restrictions, call-out start/end, and exceptions.

Track meal breaks, daily and weekly overtime, double time after 12 daily hours, and excessive hours detrimental to health or safety. Twelve hours is not a universal statutory maximum. Apply valid averaging agreements, collective agreements, exemptions, and variances by employee and effective date.
bcEmploymentStandardsProfile.operationalPolicy: Separately configure a stacking policy: avoid adjacent full staffed shifts and adjacent full standby periods. The alpha defines a full shift as eight hours and a single staffed shift limit of twelve hours as employer policy, not statute. Allow a staffed shift followed by home/mobile standby where the applicable agreement permits it; record call-outs and review actual rest and fatigue. This is an employer scheduling preference, not a BC statutory 12-hour cap.
bcEmploymentStandardsProfile.publicationGate: Re-evaluate every assignment on generate, edit, and publish. Show hard failures and unresolved review items with rule IDs and source links; never claim full legal compliance when actual call-outs or agreement data are missing.

timeRules.rule: Each location has an IANA time-zone identifier. Recurring coverage windows are defined in that location's local wall-clock time; generated assignments store both local display times and UTC instants.
Measure continuous work, on-call limits, overlap, and rest in actual elapsed minutes. Display scheduled wall-clock hours separately where they differ.

At a one-hour spring transition, a local midnight-to-midnight coverage day spans 23 elapsed hours; at a one-hour fall transition it spans 25. The roster must cover every real minute, including both occurrences of a repeated hour.

Reject a manually entered nonexistent local time during a forward jump with a clear correction prompt. Require an explicit first or second occurrence when an entered local time is ambiguous during a backward jump.

When a jurisdiction abolishes or changes clock shifts, use updated time-zone data for future schedule generation. Do not hard-code recurring March/November adjustments or retroactively change published assignment instants without review.

hardRules.rule: Do not assign an unavailable employee or overlap incompatible assignments.
Check every required qualification and any validity or eligibility constraints for a coverage slot.
Respect configured continuous on-call limits, assignment limits, rest rules, and future geographic limits when enabled.
Respect authorization and transfer policies; no cross-team change is published without required approval.
Honor applicable cross-coverage restrictions from employment groups or agreements, including department-to-department prohibitions, even when an employee has the required skill.

targetsAndPreferences.rule: Maximize coverage without falsely marking partial coverage complete; report required versus assigned people and slots.

Apply configurable relative weights from 0.01 to 1.00 to every staffed and on-call coverage interval, displayed as 1% to 100%. Weights can vary by hour, region, day, team, and requirement. A weight of 1.00 is highest scheduling importance and 0.01 is lowest. No weight may override a hard eligibility rule.

Score a proposed shift against the weighted coverage it actually supplies in each interval. A shift spanning several hours can therefore contribute differently in each hour; do not give it one flat score that hides a busy or uncovered interval.
When comparing schedules, account for both the required headcount/skill deficit and the interval weight. Report ordinary coverage counts alongside weighted coverage so low-weight gaps remain visible.

Compare feasible shift durations and patterns against required coverage, qualified employee availability, configured limits, and business preferences. A preferred 4x10 pattern may lose to 8x5 or a 12-hour pattern when the latter yields better feasible coverage.

Score candidate patterns by interval coverage weights, unmet coverage, staffing use, fairness, and business preference; show the principal tradeoffs rather than treating the preferred pattern as mandatory.
Rank eligible cross-cover candidates using configurable weights for fewer assigned shifts, minimum-shift targets, seniority, home team, and later travel.
Apply configurable shift targets and ranking preferences by employment classification; do not assume casual employees have the same shift commitment as full-time employees.
Distribute nights, weekends, holidays, and on-call fairly according to organization-defined policy.
Prefer moves from teams with surplus or lower coverage priority, but allow authorized proposals that leave a visible source shortage when policy permits.

scheduling.recommendation: Present the best eligible candidate with a short reason and before/after coverage for both teams. Expand for alternatives and complete rule explanation.
scheduling.policyEvaluation: Evaluate qualification, availability, agreement/policy scope, and assignment limits before ranking. Report a plain-language reason when a candidate is excluded, and retain the policy version used for each proposal.
scheduling.onCallPriorityExample: For the pilot, weekend 09:00-17:00 Eastern is priority 1; other weekend on-call hours are priority 2; weekday on-call hours are priority 3. These are starting weight-profile bands, not a restriction to three levels or a single weight for a whole shift. Each hour can have its own 0.01-1.00 weight and required headcount. Priority 1 denotes the highest priority. The displayed percentage expresses scheduling importance, not the probability that coverage will be achieved. Use the named Eastern time zone rather than a fixed EST offset.
scheduling.geographicExample: For Canada-wide support, local business hours in multiple regions may receive high weights. A busy Eastern morning may carry a higher weight than another region's corresponding hour. Convert regional local windows to exact instants before combining their coverage demands.
scheduling.rotationExample: A four-week employee rotation may specify seven working days in week 1, six in week 2, five in week 3, and week 4 off. Store the complete cycle and its phase for each participating employee. Validate actual hours, rest, and applicable agreements rather than inferring that the example is legal or desirable everywhere.
scheduling.example: For a requirement of one team lead and one technician, a single qualified person cannot fill both distinct-person slots unless explicitly permitted by the configured requirement; report 1 of 2 if only one slot is staffed.

A grocery employee may be eligible to cover produce while an otherwise skilled bakery employee is barred from the same move by an applicable agreement. The exact restriction is customer-configured, not built into the product.

workflows.workflow: On a fresh or reset database, seed the pilot organization and master administrator. In explicitly enabled private alpha mode, open the application already signed in as that administrator.
Configure coverage, generate draft, inspect gaps and proposed shifts, edit or request transfers, approve, publish, export.
Record or approve vacation/unavailability, recalculate affected coverage, propose eligible replacements.
Mark sick, injured, departed, or otherwise unavailable; show affected published coverage and ranked repair proposals for authorized action.
Evaluate skill and availability; compare source/destination before and after; obtain permissions/approval; record reason and outcome.
Read only from published assignments; show current and upcoming contacts within permitted visibility; export.

When weekday vacation is requested, optionally mark the adjacent weekends unavailable for on-call without counting them as vacation days. Show affected published assignments and replacement proposals during approval.

Send a proposed urgent assignment to eligible employees with a response deadline. Treat it as pending until accepted and confirmed; notify the affected person on publication and escalate unacknowledged short-notice changes under configurable policy.

Create a future-dated version of customer coverage requirements; compare capacity and candidate shift patterns against existing commitments; edit a replacement draft, coordinate cross-team approvals, review changed assignments and notice, then publish the new roster.

interfaces.view: Personal schedule, next shift and on-call status, availability and vacation information as permitted.

Spreadsheet-like weekly roster and timeline calendar with drag-and-drop creation, movement, and resizing of staffed and on-call shifts; gaps, proposals, editable drafts, scoped teams/regions, and publication controls.
interfaces.interaction: Drag across a person/time grid to create a shift; drag an assignment to another person or time; resize edges to change duration. Before committing, show local-time start/end, affected coverage and weight by interval, and any hard-rule violation or cross-team approval requirement. Permit undo before publish and provide precise form or keyboard editing for accessibility and fine adjustments.

visualDesign.rule: Use a calm, low-glare neutral and restrained pastel palette for navigation, forms, and ordinary controls. Avoid using schedule-status red, green, yellow, and orange as general site accent colors.
Reserve red, green, yellow, and orange for schedule coverage and attention states. Define their exact meanings in a persistent legend and apply them consistently across grid, calendar, and summaries.
Use stronger contrast only where attention or an action is required. Keep text, icons, grid boundaries, and selected states readable against their backgrounds in both normal and dense schedule views.

Never convey coverage state by color alone: show required/assigned counts, short labels or icons, and accessible descriptions. Verify text contrast and distinguishability for color-vision differences.

interfaces.view: People, qualifications, teams, locations, coverage rules, import, roles, and access settings.
Authorized configuration and effective-dated review of employment groups, cross-coverage permissions, restrictions, and approval rules.
Guided conditions and actions with on/off switches, scope, priority, explanation, and preview of affected assignments; available to managers or admins according to permissions.
Separate access to approved work records, pay settings, exports, and payroll integration.
interfaces.design: Use progressive disclosure so ordinary scheduling screens do not overwhelm managers with optimization settings.

onboarding.format: Downloadable Excel workbook with separate sheets and equivalent CSV templates for people (including employment classification), teams, roles/skills, qualifications, shift patterns, coverage requirements, availability, and existing assignments.
onboarding.behavior: Provide examples and field definitions; validate each row; preview the result and errors before saving; use stable employee IDs for repeat imports.

architecture.backend: Python with Django and a separate scheduling service or worker using OR-Tools.
architecture.rules: Use structured, versioned policy records evaluated by the scheduling service. Keep stable rule IDs, enable/disable state, scope, precedence, and effective dates so a guided rules builder can be added later. Add tested extension points for exceptional customer rules; avoid unrestricted user-authored code in the initial product.
architecture.database: PostgreSQL with migrations and organization-scoped data.
architecture.deployment: Docker Compose for initial private deployment; later public service can use the same application components with scalable infrastructure.
architecture.authentication: Gate automatic master-admin sign-in behind an explicit alpha configuration setting and private deployment boundary. Reject that mode in a public/production configuration. Preserve the authorization model so normal accounts and sign-in can replace bootstrap mode without changing scheduling permissions.
architecture.integration: Stage-one Teams Shifts spreadsheet export; direct API synchronization is not required.
architecture.futureDemandIntegration: Later, import time-stamped ServiceNow ticket or service-demand counts by region, skill/service, and local hour. Aggregate and review historical patterns to propose weight-profile changes; keep the approved weights versioned and manager-editable rather than changing published schedules automatically.

openDecisions.decision: Exact coverage counts, required skill combinations, shifts, breaks, and staffing data for both teams.
Specific 1%-100% hourly coverage weights and headcounts for staffed and on-call requirements; confirm whether the Eastern-time weekend example applies to Team 1 or is only an illustrative policy.
Candidate shift durations, permitted start times, weekly/rotation hour limits, and whether v0.1 compares complete pattern options or only fills a manager-selected pattern.
Notification channels, short-notice thresholds, acknowledgement deadlines, escalation recipients, and employee response workflow.
How to generate novel multiweek rotations automatically, including search boundaries, explainability, and performance for large organizations.
ServiceNow demand measure, region/service mapping, lookback period, smoothing, normalization to the 0.01-1.00 scale, and approval of suggested weight changes.
Definition of continuous on-call duration, total-hours limits, rest periods, and weekend segmentation.
Specific permission and approval matrix for manager, team lead, scheduler, and organization admin; who may accept a source-team shortage.
Ranking weights, minimum shift targets, seniority policy, and coverage priority between teams.
Whether full-time and casual classifications change minimum or maximum shifts, guaranteed hours, availability expectations, or ranking priority in the first deployment.
Which policy dimensions are required for the IT pilot and which can remain available in the model for other organizations.
For shifts crossing a clock transition, confirm operational handoff and on-call segment policy; payroll treatment of the extra or missing hour remains a later payroll decision.
Customer-specific agreement interpretation and exception workflows; configure from an approved policy supplied by the customer rather than inferring legal or union terms.
Rules-builder vocabulary, supported condition groups, precedence/conflict handling, draft testing, and manager versus admin authority to activate rules.
Employee contact fields and who may view or export them.
Exact Microsoft Teams Shifts spreadsheet fields and import behavior.
Replace alpha automatic sign-in with normal organization/user onboarding, authentication, and appropriate administrator recovery.
Geographic eligibility, travel costs, asset dependencies, payroll rules, public signup, and federation policy.

pilotAcceptance.test: Import a representative approximately 20-person dataset and generate a four-week draft for two independently configured teams.
Show fully covered and partially covered requirements by time and qualification without violating hard rules.
Apply vacation and an urgent sick call, then propose explainable eligible repairs across teams with source/destination impact.
Publish a reviewed roster and export the correct tonight-on-call lookup and Teams Shifts spreadsheet.

Generate and display coverage across a clock transition in a zone that observes one, and in a zone that no longer changes clocks; verify elapsed-minute totals and no missing or duplicate assignment interpretation.
